    Physiology

    Physiology systems.

    They cover delayed feedback, excitable tissue, the circulation, cell exchange, regulation, adaptivity, and tissues.

    AdaptiveFlowNetworkSystem(side=6, *, alpha1=1.0, alpha2=1.0, gamma=2.0, inflow=None, seed=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A square grid of vessels whose conductances adapt.

    It is fed at one corner and drained at every other node.

    The pressures balance the flows at every node, h_i = sum_j C_ij (p_i - p_j), and every conductance grows with the dissipated power and decays, dC_ij/dt = C_ij (alpha1 |p_i - p_j|^gamma - alpha2). Under a steady supply the network settles where every surviving vessel carries the same pressure drop (alpha2 / alpha1)^(1 / gamma), so the conductances grow with the flow each vessel must carry: the vessels near the source thicken into trunks and the distal ones stay thin. The system has the conductances vessels.C on the edges of the grid.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    side int

    The number of nodes along each side of the grid.

    		 6
    alpha1 float

    The growth of the conductance with the pressure drop.

    		 1.0
    alpha2 float

    The decay rate of the conductance.

    		 1.0
    gamma float

    The exponent of the pressure drop.

    		 2.0
    inflow float | None

    The flow into the source at the first corner, which the other nodes drain equally, or None for the number of edges.

    		 None
    seed int | None

    The seed of the initial conductances.

    		 0
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.physiology import AdaptiveFlowNetworkSystem
>>> AdaptiveFlowNetworkSystem(3).prepare().system_.elements[0].prepare().size_
12

    AdaptivePhaseCouplingInteraction(label, *, cells, links, N=1.0, alpha=0.0, beta=0.0, epsilon=0.01)

    Bases: NeighborInteraction

    Phase coupling of the cells of a layer through adaptive links.

    The links adapt to the phase differences they carry.

    Along the link from cell j to cell i, dphi_i/dt += -(a_ij + kappa_ij) sin(phi_i - phi_j + alpha) / N and dkappa_ij/dt = -epsilon (kappa_ij + sin(phi_i - phi_j - beta)). The phase lag alpha sets the preferred phase difference of the coupling, and the age parameter beta the rule of the adaptation.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the interaction.

    		 required
    cells Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the group of cells on the nodes.

    		 required
    links Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the group of links on the edges of the layer.

    		 required
    N Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The number of cells of the layer, which normalizes the coupling.

    		 1.0
    alpha Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]

    The phase lag of the coupling.

    		 0.0
    beta Annotated[float, ParameterSpec()]

    The age parameter of the adaptation.

    		 0.0
    epsilon Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The adaptation rate.

    		 0.01

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.physiology import AdaptivePhaseCouplingInteraction
>>> AdaptivePhaseCouplingInteraction('coupling', cells='cells', links='links', epsilon=0.3).epsilon

    AdaptiveResponderElement(label, visual=None, *, e=0.0, c=0.2, S=1.0, response_cost=0.0, restore_cost=0.0, repair_cost=0.0, prepare_cost=0.0, eta=0.5, anticipation=0.0, c0=0.2, tau=50.0, k0=0.1, kappa=0.2, price=1.0, theta=1.0, repair=5.0, upkeep=0.05, height=1.0, width=2.0, period=10.0, start=1.0)

    Bases: Element

    System that counters episodes of demand on a critical parameter.

    It pays for its response in four costs.

    The excursion of the critical parameter follows de/dt = (1 - a) s(t) - c e - k0 e, where the stimulus s is a train of episodes of height height and width width every period from start, c e is the response of a mechanism of capacity c, and a is the share of every episode that anticipation avoids. The capacity grows with the demand and decays to its baseline, dc/dt = eta e^2 - (c - c0) / tau, and the response draws the reserves, which are restored, dS/dt = -c e + kappa (1 - S). The four costs of Mobus accumulate as stocks: the response cost is the response effort c e, the restore cost the work price kappa (1 - S) of refilling the reserves, the repair cost repair (e - theta) while the excursion exceeds the damage threshold theta, and the preparedness cost the upkeep upkeep (c - c0 + a) of the extra capacity and of the anticipation.

    The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of AdaptiveResponseCostsSystem read its parameters.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the system.

    		 required
    visual VisualSpec | None

    		 None
    e Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

    The initial excursion of the critical parameter.

    		 0.0
    c Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial capacity of the response.

    		 0.2
    S Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

    The initial reserves, 1 when full.

    		 1.0
    response_cost Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial response cost.

    		 0.0
    restore_cost Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial restore cost.

    		 0.0
    repair_cost Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial repair cost.

    		 0.0
    prepare_cost Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The initial preparedness cost.

    		 0.0
    eta Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The rate at which demand builds capacity, 0 for a fixed stimulus-response.

    		 0.5
    anticipation Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The share a of every episode that anticipation avoids.

    		 0.0
    c0 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The baseline capacity.

    		 0.2

    		 0.2

    AdaptiveResponseCostsSystem(strategy='adaptive', *, height=1.0, width=2.0, period=10.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A system that meets recurring demands, by response or by anticipation.

    It meets them by stimulus-response, adaptive response, or anticipation.

    Episodes of demand push a critical parameter away from its norm, and the system counters them, after Mobus. A stimulus-response keeps its baseline capacity, so large episodes overshoot the damage threshold and cost repairs. An adaptive response builds capacity under repeated demand and loses it when demand stops, at the price of its upkeep. An anticipatory response also predicts every episode and avoids half of it. Mobus's objective is the sum of the response, restore, and repair costs over the episodes, with the preparedness cost amortized over them: adaptive response lowers it below stimulus-response by avoiding repairs, and anticipation lowers it further by cutting the response it needs. The system has the excursion organism.e, the capacity organism.c, the reserves organism.S, and the costs organism.response_cost, organism.restore_cost, organism.repair_cost, and organism.prepare_cost.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    strategy str

    'stimulus-response', 'adaptive', or 'anticipatory'.

    		 'adaptive'
    height float

    The height of the episodes of demand.

    		 1.0
    width float

    The duration of the episodes.

    		 2.0
    period float

    The time between the starts of episodes.

    		 10.0
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The strategy is unknown.

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.physiology import AdaptiveResponseCostsSystem
>>> AdaptiveResponseCostsSystem('stimulus-response').prepare().system_.elements[0].eta
0.0

    AlievPanfilovElement(label, visual=None, *, u=0.0, v=0.0, k=8.0, a=0.15, epsilon0=0.002, mu1=0.2, mu2=0.3)

    Bases: Element

    Cardiac tissue of Aliev and Panfilov, an excitable medium.

    It has the restitution of heart muscle.

    The potential follows u' = -k u (u - a) (u - 1) - u v and the recovery v' = (epsilon0 + mu1 v / (u + mu2)) (-v - k u (u - a - 1)), and a diffusion of the potential couples the cells of the tissue. The recovery rate depends on the state, so the action potential lasts longer than in the FitzHugh-Nagumo medium and its duration adapts to the pacing rate.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the tissue.

    		 required
    visual VisualSpec | None

    How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

    		 None
    u Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

    The initial potential.

    		 0.0
    v Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

    The initial recovery.

    		 0.0
    k Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The strength of the excitation.

    		 8.0
    a Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The excitation threshold.

    		 0.15
    epsilon0 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The recovery rate far from the excited state.

    		 0.002
    mu1 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The growth of the recovery rate with the recovery.

    		 0.2
    mu2 Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=open(0, oo))]

    The offset of the recovery rate.

    		 0.3

    AlievPanfilovSystem(shape=(100, 100), *, D=1.0, k=8.0, a=0.15, epsilon0=0.002, mu1=0.2, mu2=0.3, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The Aliev-Panfilov system of cardiac tissue, started from a broken wave.

    The broken wave curls into a spiral.

    A spiral wave in heart muscle is a re-entrant arrhythmia, a tachycardia, and its breakup into many waves systems fibrillation. The upper half of the tissue starts excited and its left half refractory, so the free end of the wave rotates. The system has the potential tissue.u and the recovery tissue.v.

    Parameters:

    BarkleySystem(shape=(64, 64), *, spacing=3.0, d=1.0, a=0.6, b=0.05, epsilon=0.02, gamma=1.0, label='system')

    Bases: ReactionDiffusionSystem

    Barkley's excitable medium, started from orthogonal stripes.

    The crossing of the stripes curls into a spiral wave.

    The excitation u and the recovery w start as orthogonal stripes of zeros and ones, so the excited stripe runs into recovering tissue on one side only and its free end rotates. With (a, b, d, epsilon) = (0.6, 0.05, 1, 0.02) the spiral is stable for gamma = 1. With (0.7, 0.05, 1, 0.08) and gamma = 3 it breaks up into spatiotemporal chaos. The source runs a domain of 300 by 300, and the default lattice covers 192 by 192 with a spacing of 3, wide enough for the stable spiral. The system has the excitation medium.u and the recovery medium.w.

    BranchingVesselElement(label, visual=None, *, r=1.0, l=1.0, volume=1.0, terminal=0.0, level=1.0, depth=1.0, n=2.0, r_c=1.0, l_c=1.0)

    Bases: Element

    Vessel of a space-filling branching network, sized by its level.

    Its size makes the network minimize transport energy.

    Every vessel branches into n daughters. Area-preserving branching gives the radii the ratio n^(-1/2) between levels and space filling the lengths the ratio n^(-1/3), and the capillaries at the last level depth have the same radius r_c and length l_c in every organism, so r = r_c n^((depth - level) / 2), l = l_c n^((depth - level) / 3), and the volume of the vessel is pi r^2 l.

    CardiovascularSystem(*, heart_rate=75.0, E_max=2.5, R_systemic=1.0, C_arterial=1.3, C_venous=50.0, volume=1500.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A closed lumped system of the systemic circulation.

    A left ventricle of varying elastance drives it.

    Blood leaves the ventricle through the aortic valve into the compliant arteries, flows through the systemic resistance into the veins, and returns through the mitral valve. The ventricle stiffens in systole, so the system beats, the valves open and close, and the total volume of blood stays constant. With the defaults the arterial pressure swings between about 80 and 120 mmHg. The system has the volumes ventricle.V, arteries.V, and veins.V.

    CellAdhesionInteraction(label, *, target, kinds, adhesion, temperature=1.0, area_strength=1.0, target_area=40.0, perimeter_strength=0.0, target_perimeter=0.0, state='cell', rule='metropolis', neighborhood=None, hits=1)

    Bases: RegionSamplingInteraction

    Cellular Potts sampling of a tissue, whose cells move their boundaries.

    The cells move under adhesion and area constraints.

    The energy of the Graner-Glazier model is sum_<i,j> w_ij J(t(s_i), t(s_j)) [s_i != s_j] + lambda sum_s (a_s - A)^2 + mu sum_s (p_s - P)^2, where s_i is the cell of site i, t(s) the kind of cell s, J the adhesion energy per unit contact between kinds, w_ij the weight of the contact of two sites, a_s the area of a cell, and p_s its perimeter, the weighted number of its contacts with other cells. Every sweep proposes hits copies per site of the cell of a random neighbour into a random site, accepted by the Metropolis rule at the temperature. A heterotypic adhesion above the mean of the homotypic ones sorts the kinds, the differential adhesion of Steinberg.

    CellularPottsSystem(shape=(40, 40), *, lattice='square', cell_shape=(5, 8), adhesion=DEFAULT_ADHESION, temperature=2.0, area_strength=1.0, perimeter_strength=0.0, target_perimeter=0.0, hits=1, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The cellular Potts model of a confluent tissue sorting by differential adhesion.

    Its cells are of several kinds.

    Every site of a periodic lattice belongs to one cell, and the cells start as rectangles of cell_shape sites, whose area is the target area, with kinds in equal shares at random. Label copies sample the energy sum_<i,j> w_ij J(t_i, t_j) [s_i != s_j] + lambda sum_s (a_s - A)^2 + mu sum_s (p_s - P)^2 of Nemati and de Graaf (2024), Eq. 3, extended to the adhesion J between kinds of Graner and Glazier (1992). The square lattice reads the Moore neighbourhood and the triangular lattice the six nearest neighbours, both with unit weights, and the disordered lattice is the periodic Voronoi tessellation of one jittered point per unit area, whose sites have the area of their Voronoi cell and touch along sides of weight w_ij, the length of the side over the mean length. A heterotypic adhesion above the mean of the homotypic ones raises the share of contacts between cells of one kind. The system has the states tissue.cell.

    def get_run_settings(self) -> RunSettings:
    """Return the tuned run settings, with the observables of the built parts.

    The observables are the homotypic contacts and the deviation of the areas.

    Returns:
        settings:
            The tuned run settings by name.
    """
    settings = super().get_run_settings()
    settings['observables'] = CellularPottsSystem._get_cellular_potts_observables(self._build_system())
    return settings

    ChemotacticTissueElement(label, visual=None, *, n=0.0, qx=0.0, qy=0.0, c=0.0, jx=0.0, jy=0.0, s=100.0, mu1=5000.0, mu2=5000.0, sigma=5000000.0, tau=1.0, alpha=0.33)

    Bases: Element

    Site of a tissue where cells and a chemical move with finite speeds.

    It is the hyperbolic limit of velocity jumps.

    The cell density n and its flux q, and the chemical density c and its flux j, follow Eq. (6.50) of Bellomo et al. (2017) in two dimensions with the cells as the only source of the chemical, dn/dt = -div q, dq/dt = -(s^2 / 2) grad n - mu1 q + mu2 alpha n grad c, tau dc/dt = -div j + n, and tau dj/dt = -(s^2 / 2) grad c - sigma j. Cells and chemical move at the speed s and turn at the rates mu1 and sigma, and the cells turn towards the gradient of the chemical with the sensitivity alpha. In the limit of fast turning it is the Keller-Segel model with the diffusions s^2 / (2 mu1) and s^2 / (2 sigma).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the tissue.

    		 required
    visual VisualSpec | None

    How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

    		 None
    n Annotated[float, StateSpec()]

    ClosedContourCellExchangeSystem(n_cells=8, *, r=2.5, c=0.1, p=0.5, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The exchange of signalling molecules between logistic cells.

    The cells are arranged in a closed contour.

    Every cell runs the logistic map on its concentration and takes up a share c_i of its next state from the next cell through the power map x_{i+1}^{p_i}, x_i <- (1 - c_i) r x_i (1 - x_i) + c_i x_{i+1}^{p_i}. Mihailović et al. show that an equilibrium is asymptotically stable for every coupling when every x_i lies in ((r - 1) / 2r, (r + 1) / 2r) and above p_{i-1}^(1 / (1 - p_{i-1})). In this domain the cells synchronize to a common concentration, and a chaotic environment, r near 4, desynchronizes them. The system has the concentrations cells.x, cell i + 1 next to cell i.

    Name Type Description Default
    n_cells int

    The number of cells of the contour.

    		 8

    The logistic parameter of every cell.

    The coupling of every cell to the next, one value or one per cell.

    CoagulationElement(label, visual=None, *, T=0.0, C=0.0, F=0.0, P=0.0, ka=3.0, k_half=1.0, d_t=1.0, k_c=1.0, s_c=0.1, d_c=0.05, s_f=1.0, k_p=1.0, s_p=0.02, d_p=0.1, injury=1.0, injury_time=1.0, duration=1.0)

    Bases: Element

    Coagulation cascade, thrombin amplified by positive feedback.

    Protein C switches it off, and fibrinolysis clears the clot.

    An injury of height injury from injury_time for duration activates thrombin, which activates more of itself through the feedback of the cascade, dT/dt = j(t) + ka T^2 / (k_half^2 + T^2) - (d_t + k_c C) T. Thrombin activates the inhibitor protein C, dC/dt = s_c T - d_c C, and converts fibrinogen to fibrin, dF/dt = s_f T - k_p P F. Fibrin activates plasmin, dP/dt = s_p F - d_p P, which dissolves the fibrin.

    The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of CoagulationPositiveFeedbackSystem read its parameters.

    CoagulationPositiveFeedbackSystem(*, injury=1.0, injury_time=1.0, duration=1.0, ka=3.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The coagulation cascade, an all-or-nothing burst of thrombin.

    Protein C and fibrinolysis bound the burst.

    Thrombin activates its own production through the factors of the cascade, a positive feedback that amplifies an injury above a threshold into a burst of thrombin and a clot of fibrin, while a weaker injury fades. With the default rates, the burst needs a thrombin of (ka - sqrt(ka^2 - 4)) / 2, the unstable state of the feedback. Thrombin also activates protein C, which switches the burst off, and the fibrin activates plasmin, which dissolves the clot, so the clot stays at the site and in time. The positive feedback, the off switch, and the fibrinolysis follow Konieczny et al. The system has the thrombin blood.T, the protein C blood.C, the fibrin blood.F, and the plasmin blood.P.

    		 1.0
    ka float

    The maximal rate of the positive feedback, which is bistable above 2.

    		 'system'

    ContourUptakeInteraction(label, *, target)

    Bases: CouplingInteraction

    Uptake of every cell of a contour from the next cell.

    It is x_i <- (1 - c_i) r x_i (1 - x_i) + c_i x_{i+1}^p_i.

    It is the map form of coupling to the next member of the group, with the power x_{i+1}^{p_i} of the next cell combined with the logistic map of the cell. The last cell of the contour takes up from the first.

    ExchangingCellElement(label, visual=None, *, x=1.0, alpha=1.0, beta=10.0, g=0.1, xi=0.0)

    Bases: Element

    Cell that metabolizes a substance and exchanges it with its neighbours.

    The exchange runs through gap junctions and nanotubes.

    The concentration follows dx_i/dt = -alpha_i x_i / (beta_i + x_i) + Σ_j [g (x_j - x_i) + xi A_ij x_j], where the first term is Michaelis-Menten metabolism, the one law of the cell, g the exchange coefficient of the gap junctions, and xi the strength of the tunnelling nanotubes along the same links.     FlowAdaptationInteraction(label, *, vessels, edges=(), h=(), alpha1=1.0, alpha2=1.0, gamma=2.0)

    Bases: Interaction

    Adaptation of the conductances of a transport network to its pressure drops.

    The pressure drops are those of its Kirchhoff flows.

    The nodes accumulate no fluid, so the pressures p solve the mass balance h_i = sum_j C_ij (p_i - p_j) with the external flows h, which sum to zero, at every instant. Every conductance follows dC_ij/dt = C_ij (alpha1 |p_i - p_j|^gamma - alpha2): it grows with the power dissipated along its edge and decays at a constant rate. The balance is solved numerically with the pressure of the first node fixed at zero.

    GlucoseControlElement(label, visual=None, *, G=1.0, I=1.0, N=0.5, R=0.75, k0=0.5, k_i=0.5, k_n=1.0, s_i=2.0, s_n=1.0, d_i=1.0, d_n=1.0, K=1.0, n=4.0, meal=1.0, exercise=0.8, meal_time=2.0, exercise_time=12.0, duration=2.0)

    Bases: Element

    Blood glucose held near its norm by insulin and glucagon.

    Insulin lowers it, and glucagon raises it.

    The glucose follows dG/dt = R - (k0 + k_i I) G + k_n N + u(t), where u is a meal of height meal from meal_time and an exercise of height -exercise from exercise_time, each lasting duration. High glucose secretes insulin, dI/dt = s_i h(G) - d_i I, and low glucose secretes glucagon, dN/dt = s_n (1 - h(G)) - d_n N, with the Hill switch h(G) = G^n / (G^n + K^n). The production R is set so that the norm G = K is a steady state.

    The element holds the states and parameters and has no laws of its own: the interactions of GlucoseDualHormoneControlSystem read its parameters.

    GlucoseDualHormoneControlSystem(*, glucagon=True, meal=1.0, exercise=0.8, meal_time=2.0, exercise_time=12.0, duration=2.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Blood glucose stabilised by antagonistic hormone loops.

    Insulin acts against highs and glucagon against lows.

    A meal raises the glucose and secretes insulin, which raises the uptake of glucose, and an exercise lowers it and secretes glucagon, which releases glucose from the liver. Each receptor acts in one direction only, so one loop alone corrects excursions to one side of the norm. Two opposing loops on the same quantity attenuate the excursions to both sides, after Konieczny et al. The time unit is about one hour, and the glucose is relative to its norm. The system has the glucose organism.G, the insulin organism.I, and the glucagon organism.N.

    HyperbolicChemotaxisSystem(sites=40, *, s=100.0, D_n=1.0, D_c=0.001, alpha=0.33, tau=1.0, n0=0.25, width=0.03, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Cells and a chemical moving with finite speed.

    Two bumps of cells spread and attract each other.

    The model is the hyperbolic limit of a kinetic model of cells and a chemical that change velocity at random, with the speed s and turning rates set by the diffusions D_n = s^2 / (2 mu1) and D_c = s^2 / (2 sigma) of its parabolic limit, Keller-Segel, and mu2 = mu1. Following the test of Bellomo et al. (2017, section 6.6.2), the cells start as two Gaussian bumps of mass n0 and width width at (3 width, 3 width) and (-3 width, -3 width) in the square [-0.4, 0.4]^2, here with periodic edges, the cells secrete the chemical, and all fluxes start at rest. The fluxes relax fast, so the bumps spread out at a finite speed while the cell mass 2 n0 is conserved and the chemical accumulates where the cells are. The system has the cell density tissue.n, the chemical tissue.c, and their fluxes.

    NanotubeGapJunctionExchangeSystem(graph=None, *, alpha=1.0, beta=10.0, g=0.1, xi=0.0, x=None, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The intercellular exchange of a substance on a network.

    It runs through gap junctions and tunnelling nanotubes.

    Every cell metabolizes the substance at the Michaelis-Menten rate alpha x / (beta + x) and exchanges it with its neighbours, by diffusion g (x_j - x_i) through gap junctions and by the transfer xi x_j through nanotubes. The state without substance is stable while the largest eigenvalue of xi A - g L stays below alpha / beta, where A is the adjacency and L the Laplacian of the network. Past the threshold xi_crit the nanotubes destabilize the communication and the concentrations grow. On a regular graph of degree k, xi_crit = alpha / (beta k). The system has the concentrations cells.x, one value per node.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default

    RegionSamplingInteraction(label, *, target, state, objective, move='flip', intensity=1.0, rule='metropolis', schedule='checkerboard', neighborhood=None, values=(), width=1.0, cooling=None)

    Bases: SamplingInteraction

    Monte Carlo sampling of regions of integer labels by copies of the labels of neighbours.

    The objective is a RegionScoreSpec, and the state holds integer labels from 0 on the sites of a LatticeSpace or the nodes of a NetworkSpace, whose sites of one label form a region. Every sweep proposes hits copies per site, each at a random site, of the label of one of its neighbours drawn at random, and accepts it from the change of the contact energy between regions and of the volume and surface constraints of the two regions it changes. The sampler keeps the volume and the surface of every region and updates them on every accepted copy. The neighbourhood is that of the copies and the contacts, by default the Moore neighbourhood of a square lattice, the six neighbours of a triangular lattice, or the edges of a network, whose edge attribute 'weight' weighs the contact and node attribute 'volume' the volume of a site. The schedule does not apply. The arguments are those of SamplingInteraction, with the move 'copy'.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import DiscreteTime, LatticeSpace
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import simulate
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.physiology import RegionSamplingInteraction, RegionScoreSpec
>>> class SiteElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, region: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0.0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.region = region
>>> contact = lambda first, second: np.ones(np.broadcast(first, second).shape)
>>> area = lambda labels: (1.0, 16.0)
>>> copies = RegionSamplingInteraction(
...     'copies', target='sites', state='region', objective=RegionScoreSpec(contact, area), move='copy'
... )
>>> regions = np.kron(np.arange(4).reshape(2, 2), np.ones((4, 4)))
>>> space = LatticeSpace((8, 8))
>>> sites = GroupElement('sites', element=SiteElement, space=space, on='sites', values={'region': regions})
>>> system = CompositeSystem(elements=[sites], interactions=[copies], time=DiscreteTime())
>>> final = simulate(system, until=20, random_state=0).states[-1]
>>> sorted(np.unique(final).tolist())
[0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0]

    RegionScoreSpec(contact, volume=None, surface=None, hits=1) dataclass

    Bases: BaseSpec

    Spec of an objective of a state of integer labels.

    The sites of one label form a region. The objective is sum_<i,j> w_ij c(l_i, l_j) [l_i != l_j] + sum_l a_l (V_l - A_l)^2 + b_l (S_l - B_l)^2, a cost of the boundaries between labelled regions and a quadratic penalty on the volume and the surface of every region. The first sum runs over the pairs of neighbouring sites i and j with the weight w_ij of their contact, l_i is the label of site i, V_l the volume of region l, the sum of the volumes of its sites, and S_l its surface, the sum of the weights of the contacts of its sites with sites of other labels. A label copy changes the volumes and the surfaces of only the two regions it moves a site between, so a sampler keeps them as totals per label that every accepted move updates.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    contact Callable[..., object]

    The function contact(first, second, **parameters) of two arrays of labels, which broadcast, and the parameters of the system that it names, which returns the cost per unit of boundary between regions of the labels, symmetric in the labels.

    		 required
    volume Callable[..., object] | None

    The function volume(labels, **parameters) of an array of labels, which returns the strength a_l and the target A_l of the volume constraint of every label, or None for no volume constraint.

    		 None
    surface Callable[..., object] | None

    The function surface(labels, **parameters) of an array of labels, which returns the strength b_l and the target B_l of the surface constraint of every label, or None for no surface constraint.

    		 None
    hits int

    The number of copies proposed per site and sweep.

    		 1

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationError

    The contact or a given constraint is not callable, or the number of hits is not positive.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.physiology import RegionScoreSpec
>>> contact = lambda first, second: np.ones(np.broadcast(first, second).shape)
>>> area = lambda labels: (np.ones(labels.shape), np.full(labels.shape, 16.0))
>>> RegionScoreSpec(contact, volume=area, hits=2).hits
2

    SteerableFeedbackLoopSystem(*, v=2.0, d=1.0, K=1.0, n=4.0, T=1.0, tau=0.5, steering=0.5, start=20.0, duration=20.0, label='system')

    Bases: DynamicalSystem

    A receptor-effector loop that holds a product at its set point.

    It holds it until a steering signal shifts it.

    The loop of the negative feedback system of Konieczny et al. (2023) settles at the set point where synthesis v / (1 + (x / K)^n) balances consumption d x. A steering signal, such as a bacterial toxin acting on the temperature receptors in fever, raises the sensitivity of the receptor by the factor 1 + steering, so the loop climbs to a higher set point while it acts and returns once it ends. A slow effector or a long transmission delay turns the regulation into sustained oscillations around the set point. The system has the product loop.x and the effector activity loop.e.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    v float

    The largest rate of synthesis.

    TwoCompartmentPharmacokineticsSystem(c0=1.0, *, k10=0.082, k12=0.0475, k21=0.00125, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The two-compartment pharmacokinetics of a bolus dose.

    The dose is given into the central compartment.

    The central concentration follows dUc/dt = k21 Up - (k10 + k12) Uc and the peripheral one dUp/dt = k12 Uc - k21 Up, from Uc = c0 and Up = 0. The central concentration is the bi-exponential c0 ((alpha - k21) e^(-alpha t) + (k21 - beta) e^(-beta t)) / (alpha - beta), where alpha and beta are the roots of x^2 - (k10 + k12 + k21) x + k10 k21: a fast distribution phase is followed by a slow elimination phase. The total drug Uc + Up falls only by the elimination k10 Uc. The rates are those of doxorubicin, per minute. The system has the central concentration patient.Uc and the peripheral one patient.Up.

    TwoLayerSepsisSystem(n_cells=20, *, beta=0.5 * math.pi, sigma=1.0, pathological=0.0, omega_healthy=0.0, omega_pathological=1.0, omega_immune=0.0, alpha_p=0.3 * math.pi, alpha_s=0.35 * math.pi, epsilon_p=0.03, epsilon_s=0.3, connectivity=0.5, seed=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The two-layer model of tumour disease and sepsis.

    Its parenchymal and immune cells are adaptive oscillators.

    The parenchymal layer of n_cells phase oscillators couples through fixed links a_ij, drawn as 1 with the probability connectivity, and adaptive cytokine links kappa_ij. The immune layer couples through adaptive links alone, which adapt ten times faster, and every cell couples to its partner in the other layer with strength sigma. Following Eqs. (40) and (41) of Berner et al. (2023), dphi_i/dt = omega_i - sum_j (a_ij + kappa_ij) sin(phi_i - phi_j + alpha) / N - sigma sin(phi_i - phi_i') and dkappa_ij/dt = -epsilon (kappa_ij + sin(phi_i - phi_j - beta)). The healthy state is the frequency-synchronized one, and the age parameter beta and a fraction pathological of cells with another natural frequency push the layers into desynchronized, pathological states. The system has the phases cells.phi, the parenchymal cells first and the immune cells after, and the couplings parenchymal_links.kappa and immune_links.kappa.

    Name Type Description Default

    WestBrownEnquistSystem(depth=6, *, n=2, r_c=1.0, l_c=1.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The distribution network of West, Brown, and Enquist.

    It is a space-filling tree of invariant capillaries.

    The tree branches n ways at every level down to the capillaries at level depth. The metabolic rate is proportional to the number of capillaries, n^depth, and the body mass to the blood volume, which the area-preserving and space-filling vessels make V = pi r_c^2 l_c n^depth (n^(depth / 3) - 1) / (n^(1 / 3) - 1), which grows as n^(4 depth / 3) for deep trees. So the metabolic rate scales as the mass to the power 3/4, Kleiber's law, which the exponent between consecutive depths approaches from below. A sweep over depth fits it. The system has the radii vessels.r, lengths vessels.l, and volumes vessels.volume on the edges of the tree and the observables blood_volume and capillaries of the catalog, which a run passes in observables.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    depth int

    The level of the capillaries, the number of branchings.

    n int

    The branching ratio.

    The radius of a capillary.

    l_c float

    The length of a capillary.
